why: Avro Vulcan B.2 flight-deck canopy: a flat, upright, multi-pane windscreen. The centre pair is ONE plane (y = Y_B + K (Z_B - z), independent of x) split by a centre post at x 0, out to the outer posts at |x| 0.69; each corner pane is a flat parallelogram turned 50 degrees about the outer post (the post's raked line and a horizontal direction span it: planar by construction); the two eyebrow windows lie in the flat roof plane (y = H(z)) between the mid bow and the arch, split by a centre rib; each side window lies in the vertical side wall (x = 0.86). Photographs and type descriptions of the B.2 agree on a small heavily framed canopy with flat windscreen panes, overhead eyebrow windows and small side windows; no drawing with dimensions or pane sizes was found, so the pane layout and sizes are the model's own line and UNVERIFIED against the real jet (see canopy_vulcan_b2.py). The rear crew compartment has no windows and no glass.
